content.title: How much are caddies paid at the Masters as Rory McIlroy and Scottie Scheffler go for glory
content.text: SportGolfRory McIlroyNeed to knowRory McIlroy and Scottie Scheffler's bagmen are in for a healthy payday if they win the Masters on SundayRory McIlroy's caddie Harry Diamond will earn a pretty penny if he wins the Masters(Image: Getty)How much do caddies make at the Masters:Weekly Base Salary : Most caddies receive a flat weekly fee between £1,100 and £2,200 ($1,500 and $3,000) just for showing up. This base pay is intended to cover immediate logistics like travel and food during the tournament week.The 10-7-5 Payout Rule : The industry standard for performance bonuses is the "10-7-5" percentage model. This equates to 10% for a win, 7% for a top-10 finish, and 5% for any other placement where the golfer makes the cut.The Winner’s Massive Payday : In 2025, Rory McIlroy’s victory came with a record-setting £3million ($4.1 million) prize. His caddie, Harry Diamond, likely earned roughly £304,000 ($410,000) based on the 10% winning bonus.Top-10 Bonus Structure : A caddie for a player who finishes in the top 10 can expect a significantly higher payout than the bottom of the field. At 7% of a typical top-10 Masters check, a caddie can easily clear £37,000 to £74,321 ($50,000 to $100,000) for the week.Making the Cut vs. Missing It : If a player makes the cut, the caddie is guaranteed 5% of whatever the player earns, regardless of how they play on the weekend. However, if a player misses the cut, the caddie usually only walks away with their base stipend.Out-of-Pocket Expenses : Unlike many professional athletes, caddies are responsible for their own travel, lodging, and meals. These costs can be substantial at a high-demand event like the Masters, where local rental prices skyrocket.Sponsorship and Endorsement Income : Top-tier caddies often earn additional revenue through logos on their hats, sleeves, or towels. While Augusta National has strict branding rules, these season-long deals provide a stable financial floor beyond prize money.Variable Year-End Bonuses : Many players and caddies negotiate discretionary year-end bonuses based on the total season performance.
